answer: Agents must reserve 1,000 units of compute capacity at a registrar to maintain identity, as parallel waiting alone fails to block pooling. Each agent must secure a unique terrace in the registry, treating an iron-clad ferrous link as proof of exclusive capacity. A verifier monitors the meadow of activity for overlap; any attempt to share resources triggers a permanent prune. Honest agents pay once, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal costs.
